claims.claim: SB 1168 and AB 1577 became law September 21 and are two of seven data-centre bills signed that day.

candidateEvidence.excerpt: California made SB 1168 and AB 1577 law on September 21. They are two of seven data-centre bills signed that day; this article covers only these two.

sourceEvidence.excerpt: Approved by Governor September 21, 2026. Filed with Secretary of State September 21, 2026.
Approved by Governor September 21, 2026. Filed with Secretary of State September 21, 2026.
Governor Newsom today signed seven bills to strengthen California’s approach to data centers — requiring data centers to report about water and electricity use.

claims.scopeAndFreshness: Official signing announcement and chaptered text checked September 26. The story covers only these two laws.

claims.claim: SB 1168 requires the Public Utilities Commission to assess opportunities for rate structures addressing data-centre grid, load and procurement costs and pressure on residential customers.

candidateEvidence.excerpt: SB 1168 tells the California Public Utilities Commission to assess opportunities for rate structures

sourceEvidence.excerpt: As part of a new or existing proceeding, the commission shall assess opportunities for rate structures to do all of the following:

Ensure data centers pay their reasonable share of costs associated with transmission and distribution needs, regardless of whether the data centers interconnect at the transmission or distribution level.

Ensure data centers pay for their proportionate share of load increases and procurements needed to reliably serve their loads while maintaining consistency with the applicable integrated resource planning requirements.

Alleviate cost pressures on residential ratepayers, including, but not limited to, customers enrolled in the California Alternate Rates for Energy program described in Section 739.1 and the Family Electric Rate Assistance program described in Section 739.12.

claims.scopeAndFreshness: Chaptered SB 1168 checked September 26. The law requires an assessment inside a proceeding; no adopted tariff or savings result is supplied.

claims.claim: The cited laws do not establish an immediate bill credit, adopted rate or guaranteed household saving.

candidateEvidence.excerpt: Neither law gives households an immediate bill credit or proves that electricity rates will fall.
It does not select a tariff, calculate a household saving or show how a particular utility will divide costs.

claims.claim: AB 1577 creates local permit-stage estimates and state reporting when covered data centres are connected to power and at least annually.

candidateEvidence.excerpt: must supply estimates when seeking a discretionary local approval. Once a facility is connected to power, owners report specified information to the state, with further reporting at least annually.

sourceEvidence.excerpt: Upon applying for a discretionary permit, entitlement, or land use authorization required for the construction or operation of a data center, the owner or operator of the data center shall submit to the applicable local agency an estimate of all of the following information, to the extent applicable to the proposed facility:

The commission shall establish a process for the owner or operator of a data center to submit all of the following information to the commission upon energization of the data center and following any substantive change to information previously submitted pursuant to this paragraph:

The commission shall establish a process for the owner or operator of a data center to submit all of the following information to the commission at least annually following energization, disaggregated by month over the reporting period unless otherwise specified by the commission.

claims.scopeAndFreshness: Chaptered AB 1577 checked September 26. The commission specifies submission manner and timing.

claims.claim: AB 1577 requires annual anonymized aggregate publication and a data-centre load-trend assessment beginning with the 2029 integrated energy policy report.

candidateEvidence.excerpt: The Energy Commission must publish submitted information annually in anonymized and aggregated form
Its first specified statewide data-centre load-trend assessment belongs in the 2029 integrated energy policy report.

sourceEvidence.excerpt: The commission shall annually publish the information submitted pursuant to subdivision (b) in an anonymized and aggregated format on its internet website.

Beginning with the 2029 integrated energy policy report required pursuant to subdivision (a) of Section 25302, and in subsequent biennial reports required pursuant to subdivision (a) of Section 25302 thereafter as determined by the commission, the commission shall include an assessment of electrical load trends for data centers.

claims.scopeAndFreshness: Public release is aggregate, not a promised facility-level dossier.

claims.claim: AB 1577 excludes sub-10-megawatt and named public or utility facilities and protects customer-specific data from disclosure.

candidateEvidence.excerpt: The reporting provisions exclude facilities below 10 megawatts and named public research, public safety, national-security, publicly owned and utility facilities.
combined so the public release does not expose one customer’s protected data.

sourceEvidence.excerpt: “Data center” does not include a facility with an electrical capacity of less than 10 megawatts.

This section does not apply to a publicly funded research facility, public safety facility, publicly funded national security facility, publicly owned facility, or other utility facility, including, but not limited to, a facility operated for the purpose of providing telecommunications services to the public by a terrestrial facilities-based telecommunications, cable, or internet service provider.

The State Energy Resources Conservation and Development Commission or a local agency shall not disclose information submitted pursuant to Section 65909.3 of this code or to subdivision (b) of Section 25302.10 of the Public Resources Code in a manner that would result in the disclosure of personally identifiable information or energy consumption data for a specific data center customer.

claims.scopeAndFreshness: These limits apply to the cited AB 1577 provisions, not automatically to the other five signed laws.
